`resetall
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
`default_nettype none

module priority_encoder #(
    parameter WIDTH = 4,
    parameter LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY = 0,
    parameter LEVELS = WIDTH > 2 ? $clog2(WIDTH) : 1,
    parameter W = 2**LEVELS
)(
    input  wire [WIDTH-1:0] input_unencoded,
    output wire output_valid,
    output wire [$clog2(WIDTH)-1:0] output_encoded,
    output wire [WIDTH-1:0] output_unencoded
);

generate
if (WIDTH == 256 && LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY == 0 && LEVELS == 8 && W == 256) begin : fast_256
    wire [15:0] group_valid;
    wire [15:0] group_allow;
    wire [15:0] group_winner;
    wire [15:0] local_winner [0:15];
    wire [3:0] local_code [0:15];
    wire [15:0] code_terms [0:3];
    genvar g, b, k;

    for (g = 0; g < 16; g = g + 1) begin : groups
        assign group_valid[g] = |input_unencoded[g*16 +: 16];
        if (g == 15) begin : top_group
            assign group_allow[g] = 1'b1;
        end else begin : lower_group
            assign group_allow[g] = ~(|group_valid[15:g+1]);
        end
        assign group_winner[g] = group_valid[g] & group_allow[g];

        for (b = 0; b < 16; b = b + 1) begin : bits_in_group
            if (b == 15) begin : top_bit
                assign local_winner[g][b] = input_unencoded[g*16+b];
            end else begin : lower_bit
                assign local_winner[g][b] = input_unencoded[g*16+b]
                    & ~(|input_unencoded[g*16+15:g*16+b+1]);
            end
            if (g == 0 && b == 0) begin : default_bit
                // The reference shift produces bit zero even on an empty input.
                assign output_unencoded[g*16+b] = ~(|input_unencoded[255:1]);
            end else begin : selected_bit
                assign output_unencoded[g*16+b] = group_allow[g] & local_winner[g][b];
            end
        end

        assign local_code[g][0] = |(local_winner[g] & 16'haaaa);
        assign local_code[g][1] = |(local_winner[g] & 16'hcccc);
        assign local_code[g][2] = |(local_winner[g] & 16'hf0f0);
        assign local_code[g][3] = |input_unencoded[g*16+8 +: 8];
        for (k = 0; k < 4; k = k + 1) begin : code_columns
            assign code_terms[k][g] = group_allow[g] & local_code[g][k];
        end
    end

    assign output_valid = |group_valid;
    assign output_encoded[0] = |code_terms[0];
    assign output_encoded[1] = |code_terms[1];
    assign output_encoded[2] = |code_terms[2];
    assign output_encoded[3] = |code_terms[3];
    assign output_encoded[4] = |(group_winner & 16'haaaa);
    assign output_encoded[5] = |(group_winner & 16'hcccc);
    assign output_encoded[6] = |(group_winner & 16'hf0f0);
    assign output_encoded[7] = |group_valid[15:8];
end else begin : reference_parameters
    wire [W-1:0] input_padded = {{W-WIDTH{1'b0}}, input_unencoded};
    wire [W/2-1:0] stage_valid [LEVELS-1:0];
    wire [W/2-1:0] stage_enc [LEVELS-1:0];
    genvar l, n;

    for (n = 0; n < W/2; n = n + 1) begin : loop_in
        assign stage_valid[0][n] = |input_padded[n*2+1:n*2];
        if (LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin : lsb_pair
            assign stage_enc[0][n] = !input_padded[n*2];
        end else begin : msb_pair
            assign stage_enc[0][n] = input_padded[n*2+1];
        end
    end

    for (l = 1; l < LEVELS; l = l + 1) begin : loop_levels
        for (n = 0; n < W/(2*2**l); n = n + 1) begin : loop_compress
            assign stage_valid[l][n] = |stage_valid[l-1][n*2+1:n*2];
            if (LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin : lsb_compress
                assign stage_enc[l][(n+1)*(l+1)-1:n*(l+1)] =
                    stage_valid[l-1][n*2] ?
                    {1'b0, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+1)*l-1:(n*2)*l]} :
                    {1'b1, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+2)*l-1:(n*2+1)*l]};
            end else begin : msb_compress
                assign stage_enc[l][(n+1)*(l+1)-1:n*(l+1)] =
                    stage_valid[l-1][n*2+1] ?
                    {1'b1, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+2)*l-1:(n*2+1)*l]} :
                    {1'b0, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+1)*l-1:(n*2)*l]};
            end
        end
    end

    assign output_valid = stage_valid[LEVELS-1];
    assign output_encoded = stage_enc[LEVELS-1];
    assign output_unencoded = 1 << output_encoded;
end
endgenerate
endmodule

`resetall
",
  "bottleneck": "The reference builds an eight-level binary priority tree and then derives the one-hot output from the encoded result. Paths to output_unencoded can therefore traverse priority selection followed by binary-to-one-hot decoding. Upper-level valid signals also control multiple encoded-bit muxes.",
  "rewrite": "For the specified configuration, partition the input into sixteen 16-bit groups. Compute local winners and higher-group suppression in parallel. Produce output_unencoded directly from these signals, without waiting for output_encoded. Encode group winners and selected local codes using parallel masked reductions. Retain the original implementation for other parameter configurations, including explicit LEVELS or W overrides.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The main expected improvement is elimination of the serial encode-then-decode path to the 256-bit one-hot output. Parallel group suppression also replaces the full-width encoded mux tree. Numerical arrival-time improvement is not measured here; confirmation requires the specified SKY130HD mapping, STA, and electrical checks.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Local winner logic, group suppression, and encoded reductions trade some shared mux-tree logic for parallel logic. Group-allow nets may require buffering because they drive local outputs and encoded terms. No storage or added latency is introduced. Mapped area relative to the 8862.124480 um2 cap has not been measured.",
  "functional_boundaries": "For WIDTH=256 and LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY=0, every nonzero input selects its highest asserted bit. An all-zero input produces output_valid=0, output_encoded=0, and output_unencoded=256'b1, matching the reference's unqualified shift. All input bits remain arbitrary binary values. Module name, port widths and unsigned declarations, parameter defaults, and fallback truncation behavior are preserved. The implementation is entirely combinational, requires no helper modules, and contains no assumptions, assertions, undefined outputs, or CRC interfaces."
}
